title: Entropy-mediated queue resilience and starvation dampening for continuous batcher
author: Avery Collins
description: Motivation: In some production workloads we observed long-tail starvation where low-cost KV-heavy requests were repeatedly preempted by batches with high prefix similarity, creating both fairness and SLO violations on small requests. Prior approaches (soft reservations, aging credits) reduced but did not eliminate pathological cases when request arrival patterns were bursty and high-variance. This PR implements an entropy-mediated admission and resilience layer for the continuous batcher that: 1) computes a lightweight per-queue entropy score over recent sequence-token distributions to detect low-diversity (highly coalescible) traffic, 2) applies a bounded decayable urgency credit to queues that have been starved, 3) uses an admission threshold that dynamically blends entropy and urgency to prefer admitting small/latency-sensitive queues when the global batch composition would otherwise starve them, and 4) aligns KV prefetch hints and kernel slice flags so the runtime can co-locate short KV-heavy slots onto optimized execution paths. Design summary: The admission controller runs in the batcher event loop and maintains a rolling sketch (count-min + age-decay) of token-prefix signatures per queue to estimate entropy. Entropy is normalized per-model and sequence-length bucket. Urgency credit accrues when a queue has been bypassed for a configurable number of scheduling epochs and decays with a tunable half-life. The final admit_score = alpha * normalized_urgency + (1 - alpha) * (1 - normalized_entropy) where alpha is adjusted by load (lower alpha under heavy throughput so we preserve batching efficiency). We limit admitted extra slots per batch via a resilience_budget to bound tail cost. Implementation highlights: - New module runtime/scheduler/entropy_admitter.rs (Rust) with unit-tested sketch and a fast vectorized normalization path. - Urgency credit logic factored into runtime/scheduler/decay_credit.rs for reuse in preemption paths. - Continuous batcher hooks to consume admit_score and to annotate BatchMetadata with admit_reason for observability. - KV prefetch alignment: batcher sets lightweight kernel_hint flags in runtime/kv/cache_prefetcher.rs to prefer the 'short-kv' execution slice for admitted short requests. Tests and validation: - microbench bench/perf/queue_fairness_bench.py reproduces the previous starvation pattern and demonstrates median latency reduction for small requests. - tests/scheduler/test_entropy_admit.py covers edge cases: model-switch, sequence-length bucket boundary, and concurrent queue churn. - End-to-end perf run in CI (perf/integration) measured on a representative 8-GPU dev cluster. Results: single-stage canary at 20% traffic reduced 95th percentile latency for the small-request cohort by 28%-35% depending on model family, with overall token-cost increase of 1.8% and throughput drop within 1.2% of baseline under the tested mix. Rollout: feature gated under flag runtime.features.entropy_admit default off. Rollout steps: 1) lab + canary at 5% (1 day), 2) staged canary 20% (3 days), 3) broader regional ramp with monitoring (7 days). Metrics to watch: small_request_p95, admitted_slots_ratio, batch_coalescence_index, kv_slice_utilization, token_cost_per_minute. Backout: disable flag and revert kernel_hint path alone if unexpected cost regression. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for entropy sketch and credit decay - [x] Integration bench reproducing failure mode - [x] Observability: added admit_reason tag and new dashboard tiles - [x] Feature flag and safe defaults - [x] Performance evaluation and canary plan - [x] Docs: docs/notes/entropy-admission.md Links: Linear ENG-14208 (investigate starvation cases), ENG-14209 (rollout), internal doc https://linear.company/ENG-14208/details (for runbook).

review_thread: Priya Sharma: Can you explain the cost-bound on resilience_budget? It reads like it could grow unbounded under pathological churn.

Avery Collins: resilience_budget is strictly capped per-batch and the controller reduces alpha when global batch size exceeds the budget; added comment and test to demonstrate the cap (see entropy_admitter.rs).
Diego Morales: perf numbers look good, can you share the distribution across model families? The PR only has aggregate numbers.
Avery Collins: added breakdown in bench results: LLaMA-13B: p95 small-req -30%, Mistral-7B: -28%, long-context models show <2% change in tail. Added bench output to PR description and artifacts.
Lena Fischer: nit: prefer consistent naming for kernel_hint enum variants (short_kv vs SHORT_KV); updated to SCREAM_CASE in the patch.
Priya Sharma: Approve after you add an e2e smoke to ensure admit_reason tag survives routing and logging.
Avery Collins: added tests/scheduler/e2e_admit_smoke.sh and extended integration test to assert admit_reason on logs.
Priya Sharma: CI showed intermittent flake on bench harness, post-merge please watch ci/perf for one additional run.
Avery Collins: re-ran perf CI, resolved race in bench harness by tightening sleeps in test harness.
Diego Morales: LGTM, approving for merge.
release_notes: Adds an entropy-mediated admission controller to the continuous batcher that reduces small-request starvation. Opt-in via runtime.features.entropy_admit (default off). Observability: admit_reason tag and new dashboard tiles. Expected p95 improvement for small-request cohort; small token-cost tradeoff under certain mixes.
perf_summary: Canary at 20%: small-request p95 down 28-35%, overall token-cost +1.8%, throughput -1.2% under bench mix. Bench artifacts attached to PR.
rollout_plan: Start with lab + 5% canary (24h), expand to 20% (72h) if stable, regional ramp with metrics gating; emergency rollback via feature flag or revert of kernel_hint path.
